algorithm.title: Evaluation of Hip Pain in Adults

cell.label: Fever, chills, skin infection, recent joint injection or surgery, or hip replacement?
History of cancer, weight loss, or night pain?
Steroid use, heavy alcohol use, sickle cell disease, or past fracture or dislocation?
Where is the pain?
cell.path: Groin pain, stiffness, and painful internal rotation, age 45 or older
Lateral hip pain with tenderness over the greater trochanter
Groin pain with clicking or catching in a younger, active adult

cell.label: X-ray (AP pelvis and lateral hip). If negative but unable to bear weight, MRI for occult fracture.
Suspect septic arthritis or prosthetic joint infection. ESR, CRP, joint aspiration; urgent orthopedic referral.
X-ray; MRI if negative to evaluate for metastasis or primary bone tumor.
X-ray; noncontrast MRI if negative to rule out avascular necrosis.
Hip osteoarthritis. Clinical diagnosis; X-ray only if uncertain. Exercise, weight loss, NSAIDs.
Greater trochanteric pain syndrome (gluteal tendinopathy). Exercise therapy; injection if needed.
Femoroacetabular impingement or labral tear. X-ray, physical therapy; MRI arthrogram if it persists.
Consider stress fracture (runners, osteoporosis), hernia, or abdominal or pelvic causes. MRI if pain persists.

footnotes.footnote: Hip pain may be referred from the lumbar spine, abdomen, or pelvis.
Hip arthroscopy has limited benefit for degenerative disease.
